descriptionText: Using contains() with a space-separated string to check if a user-controllable value matches allowed values can be bypassed. For example, contains('refs/heads/main refs/heads/develop', github.ref) is intended to check if a branch is either main or develop, but an attacker can bypass this by creating a branch like 'refs/heads/main/malicious' or 'refs/heads/main ' (with trailing space). The contains() function performs substring matching, not exact matching, so these attacker-controlled values will match even though they're not in the intended set. This is especially dangerous when the second argument is a user-controllable context like github.ref, github.actor, github.head_ref, env.*, or inputs.*. Use explicit equality checks (github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/develop') or a proper JSON array (contains(fromJSON('["refs/heads/main", "refs/heads/develop"]'), github.ref)) instead.
